name: Amaranth Leaf Spot
description: A fungal leaf disease causing circular to irregular spots on amaranth leaves, reducing their market value and photosynthetic capacity. It is common in humid growing conditions across West Africa.
symptoms: Small circular brown spots on leaves
Spots enlarging with concentric rings and yellow halos
Lesions coalescing into large necrotic areas
causes: Alternaria amaranthi and Cercospora spp. fungi
Dense planting with poor air circulation
treatments: Apply copper-based fungicides at first symptoms
Spray mancozeb or chlorothalonil at 7-10 day intervals
Use neem oil spray as organic alternative
prevention: Space plants adequately for air circulation
Avoid overhead irrigation — use drip irrigation or watering at base
Practice crop rotation with non-leafy crops
Remove and destroy crop debris after harvest
Use well-drained beds to reduce humidity
